edges_sub_pix — 2D contour op

• Data kinds: image → contour

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "edges_sub_pix", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: edges_sub_pix (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

• GPU: yes (mechanical GPU path from the allow-list, CuPy). device="auto" chooses the GPU from the measured size (4,194,304 pixels) up

Usage

Sub-pixel-accurate edge contour extraction. Computes the gradient and its normal direction (gradient_normals), thins it to one pixel by non-maximum suppression (as in Canny: only pixels stronger than both neighbours along the normal), links the pixels above the threshold (0.15+0.5*a, strength normalised by the maximum gradient) into contours ordered along the curve (split into separate contours at branch points; a closed edge is closed at its start point), and refines each point along the normal to sub-pixel position by parabola fitting (subpixel_refine_edges, an implementation shared with the same-named op on the ops side -- a 2026-09-02 fix made it genuinely sub-pixel; the old implementation returned integer pixel coordinates). Equivalent to HALCON's edges_sub_pix (Extract sub-pixel precise edges using Deriche, Lanser, Shen, or Canny filters.).

The points of each contour are in order along the curve (neighbouring points about 1 px apart), so length_xld measures the length of the edge and area_center_xld / circularity_xld the shape enclosed by a closed edge (a disc with r = 18 px gives length_xld about 113 px = 2πr).

★Until 2026-11-03 the pixels of the 2–3 px wide band above the threshold were put into one contour in raster order — the same disc gave length_xld 2508 px (the points zig-zagged row by row). Quantities that do not depend on point order (line fits such as fit_line_contour_xld) stay close to their earlier values.

a sets the edge-strength threshold. b is unused.

Raises:

FsValueError: an image containing NaN / inf.
